newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips fall, but high tech issues up modestly.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips fall, but high tech issues up modestly.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell on Monday but high-technology and small issues managed modest gains as investors struggled for clues as to where stocks and interest rates were headed.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 27.18 points to 8,166.86 just after 1 p.m. EDT (1400 GMT), but the Nasdaq composite index, heavily weighted with high-tech issues, rose 8.27 points to 1,602.60.
In the broader market, declining issues outnumbered gainers by about a 15-13 margin on moderate New York Stock Exchange volume of about 252 million shares.
The Russell 2000 index of small company stocks edged up 0.22 of a point to 414.43.

"The Dow is down a little but the broader market is exhibiting good strength," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "A lot of smaller, Nasdaq-oriented issues seem to be doing well. Money continues to filter into secondary issues."

Investors paused for breath after stocks fell last week following stronger-than-expected economic reports that revived fears that the Federal Reserve would raise short-term interest rates in a bid to ward off inflation.

Bond prices, which fell with stocks last week, continued to weaken on Monday. The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell about half a point and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, rose to 6.49 perent from 6.45 percent on Friday.

"The bond market has been weak the last two days but the stock market doesn't want to quit," Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt, said. "Nasdaq is strong and there is still a lot of momentum on the buy side."
Technology, transport and small-capitalisation isses firmed while stocks in financial, utility, banking and insurance sectors declined.
Investors noted that that few major economic reports were due this week after a strong July jobs report and other data gave investors inflation jitters last week.
But Sam Stovall, an analyst for Standard & Poor's Industry Reports, said investors might spend this week jockeying for position ahead of key inflation data coming next week.
"People are wondering if this is just the beginning of data which is going to cause some concern about higher interest rates and inflation," he said.

The unemployment rate fell to the lowest in nearly a quarter century last month as the economy created new jobs at a surprisingly fast clip, the government said on Friday, and coupled with reports of unexpectedly strong manufacturing activity, sent financial markets reeling on concerns that economic growth might pick up enough to spark inflation.
Among individual issues, Alpha-Beta fell 4-5/16 to 6-1/2 after it said its Betafectin showed no stastical significance in a test to see if it could reduce serious infections.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks added 0.52 of a point to 947.66.
The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.04 to 644.23.
